title: ops-telemetry-sketchbook-threshold-experiments-and-trace-hooks
body:
Quick sketchbook: what I want to try for the next 2 sprints. Mostly notes-to-self and quick test plans. Not a polished playbook yet — focus on actionable experiments that can reduce alert noise and make tenant throttles visible without shredding query budgets.

Context and problem statement
- We keep getting noisy pager alerts for tenant throttle/cold-cache events; many are duplicates and several are false positives caused by noisy aggregations.
- Need compact probe + trace hooks to tie SLI blips to cache eviction events and routing fallbacks.
- Goal: cut median investigation time from ~45m -> ~15m for throttle incidents, and remove 30% of redundant alerts.

Primary hypotheses
1) A small set of tuned thresholds on low-cardinality rollup metrics plus a session-linked trace sample will catch true incidents without alert storms.
2) Adaptive sampling that increases trace rate on throttle-signal co-occurrence reduces time-to-root-cause with minimal trace budget change.
3) Correlating a "prefetch_heat" index with per-tenant cold_start_rate surfaces tenants that trigger failures.

Core metrics to add / standardize (defn sketches)
- prefetch_heat_index: rolling 5m score in [0..1] representing prefetch success weighted by recency. formula: (successful_prefetches_weighted / expected_prefetches_weighted). Use EWMA with alpha=0.2. low values => cold starts.
- tenant_cold_start_rate: count(cold_start_event)/count(request) per tenant, 5m. cardinality: tenant_id. rollup: p50/p95 across tenants.
- eviction_spike_rate: rate(kv_eviction_count) over 1m windows; annotate with node and pool.
- throttle_fanout_factor: number of clients impacted by a throttle window normalized by active_clients. High values => system-level issue.
- batching_efficiency_ratio: tokens_processed / (requests * avg_batch_size) — useful to detect regression after batching config changes.
- ttfb_token_quantile: time-to-first-token per-request quantiles (p50/p95/p99) correlated with first_kv_lookup_latency.
- per_token_cost_estimate: derived cost estimate per-token (simple multiply of token_count * unit_cost) — we will keep as approximate to flag cost anomalies.

Trace anchoring patterns (span conventions)
- span.operation: inference.request; tags: tenant_id, model_id, route, batch_id, kvcache_hit(true|false), prefetch_tag
- span.children: kvcache.lookup spans should include keys: key_count, lookup_latency_ms, eviction_flag
- sampling hints: if eviction_spike_rate > X AND tenant_cold_start_rate > Y then increase trace sample multiplier for that tenant to 30% for 10m.
- synthetic trace breadcrumbs: add synthetic trace id in probe responses so we can correlate probe-panel events with traces (small sample).

Dashboard wireframe notes (compact operator-first layout)
Top row: incident-at-a-glance\- mini timeline (1h/6h/24h) showing throttle_fanout_factor, eviction_spike_rate, and prefetch_heat_index (stacked). Clicking a window narrows session_id filter.
Second row: tenant breakouts\- sparklines and p95 ttfb per-tenant (top 20 by traffic); hover shows tenant_cold_start_rate delta vs baseline.
Third row: trace anchors + recent spans\- list of most recent sampled traces with quick links to trace UI and pinned span summaries (kvcache miss count, eviction_flag, first_kv_latency).
Bottom: signal correlation matrix (heatmap)\- pairwise correlation over sliding 24h for eviction_spike_rate, ttfb_token_quantile_p95, batching_efficiency_ratio, per_token_cost_estimate.

Alerting and threshold experiments (plan)
- Baseline: existing alerts (very noisy).
- Experiment A (Low-card rollup): create two-stage alerts: 1) soft alert if eviction_spike_rate > 3x baseline for 5m (channel: ops-notify, severity low), 2) hard alert if eviction_spike_rate > 5x baseline AND throttle_fanout_factor > 0.2 (pager).
- Experiment B (Tenant gating): create tenant-scoped soft alerts for tenant_cold_start_rate if tenant contribution to overall error rate > 0.5% AND tenant traffic > threshold. Suppresses tiny tenants.
- Experiment C (Trace-driven escalation): when soft alert fires, automatically bump trace sampling for the affected tenant/pool and attach synthetic probe ids to help correlate. If traces confirm eviction->throttle chain, escalate.
- Evaluation window: run each experiment for 2 weeks; measure false positive rate, median time-to-resolve, and trace budget consumption.

Quick investigation runbook (operator-first)
1) Open dashboard, inspect top-row event timeline for the selected window.
2) If eviction_spike_rate high: check node distribution -> are evictions concentrated? If yes, narrow to node and check recent deploys.
3) If tenant_cold_start_rate high for one tenant: open trace list for that tenant, look for repeated kvcache.lookup with eviction_flag=true.
4) Check batching_efficiency_ratio — a sudden drop often co-occurs with routing fallback.
5) If correlation heatmap shows strong eviction <-> ttfb p95, escalate to infra and consider emergency prefetchtune.

Sample SQL snippets for quick panels (replace metrics table names as appropriate)
-- eviction_spike_rate per minute
SELECT floor(extract(epoch from ts)/60) as minute, sum(eviction_count) as evictions FROM telemetry.kv_evictions WHERE ts > now() - interval '6 hours' GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute DESC LIMIT 360;

-- per-tenant cold start rate (5m)
SELECT tenant_id, sum(case when cold_start then 1 else 0 end)::float / nullif(count(*),0) as cold_start_rate FROM telemetry.requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 minutes' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY cold_start_rate DESC LIMIT 50;

Implementation notes and constraints
- Keep low-cardinality rollups in the main dashboard for query-cost control. Heavy cardinality (per-tenant spans) only on demand or sampled.
- Trace budget: keep baseline low (0.5%) but allow temporary multipliers per-tenant up to 30% for short windows. Track cost delta daily.
- Prefetch_heat_index must be computed at ingestion time if possible (store as tag) to avoid repeated heavy queries.

Open questions / decisions to take
- numeric thresholds: what is eviction_spike_rate multiplier that balances sensitivity and noise? (start with 3x/5x for soft/hard).
- how long should tenant-level elevated sampling persist? (10m vs 30m).
- where to surface suppression windows in UI so SREs know silence windows exist.

Action items (next 10 days)
- [ ] Jesse: prototype dashboard tiles (top row + heatmap) using existing dashkit components (due 2026-02-18).
- [ ] Ravi: add prefetch_heat_index to ingestion pipeline as tag (proof-of-concept) (due 2026-02-24).
- [ ] Eleni: implement trace multiplier hook on alert soft-fire (hook into trace-config service) (due 2026-03-01).
- [ ] Maya: run synthetic probe campaign to validate correlation with traces and tune thresholds (due 2026-03-05).

Notes to self
- Keep the first demo very narrow: one pool, one tenant cohort, dashboard focused on last 6h. Too many knobs will kill the experiment.
- Remember to include cost telemetry in the evaluation matrix — we may get better signal at much higher cost.

References and links
- Confluence runbook draft: CONFLUENCE-OBS-RTF-42 (linked above)
- Related Jira: JIRA-OBS-1182 (tenant sampling enhancements)
- Example trace annotations: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-scripts/blob/main/trace-anchors.md

End of sketchbook entry. Will iterate after first experiment results.
